meta.titre: Pastry and Cake Making: Methods, Ingredients and Faults
meta.sous_theme: Cake methods, role of ingredients, shortcrust pastry and common faults

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: For a birthday in Douala a baker's cake may cost several thousand FCFA, but a student who masters the creaming method can bake a good sponge at home. Cakes and pastry test skill: a small mistake in mixing or in the oven gives a flat, cracked or heavy result. The GCE asks for the methods, the work of each ingredient and the causes of faults.

items: Gas bubbles expand when heated and make a mixture rise.
The basic ingredients of a cake are flour, fat, sugar, eggs and a raising agent.

sections.titre: Cake and pastry making: ingredients, methods and faults
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Role of the ingredients in a cake

| Ingredient | Role |
|---|---|
| Flour | gives structure when its starch and protein set in the heat |
| Fat | makes the cake tender, adds flavour, holds air when creamed |
| Sugar | sweetens, browns the crust, holds air when creamed |
| Eggs | trap air, set the structure, bind, add colour, flavour and nutrients |
| Raising agent | baking powder gives carbon dioxide when wet and hot |
| Liquid (milk) | gives a soft dropping consistency |

### Methods of making cakes

| Method | How it is done | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Creaming | beat fat and sugar until pale and fluffy, add beaten egg a little at a time, then fold in sifted flour | sandwich cake, queen cakes |
| Rubbing-in | rub fat into flour with the fingertips until like fine breadcrumbs, then add other ingredients | rock cakes, scones |
| Whisking | whisk eggs and sugar until thick and pale, then fold in flour gently | fatless sponge |
| Melting | melt fat and sugar or syrup, then mix with flour | gingerbread |

Air is added by sifting flour, creaming, whisking and folding. Steam and carbon dioxide also make cakes rise.

### Shortcrust pastry
Use half as much fat as flour by weight. Use cold fat, rub it in lightly, mix with a little cold water to a firm dough, handle as little as possible, let the dough rest, and bake in a fairly hot oven. Warm hands, too much water or too much handling make the pastry hard and greasy.

variantes.nom: Faults in cakes and their causes
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a cake has gone wrong and the question asks for the cause or for ways to prevent the fault.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
| Fault | Likely causes |
|---|---|
| Risen high and cracked on top | oven too hot, so the crust sets before the middle has risen; too much raising agent; tin too small |
| Sunk in the middle | oven door opened too early; too much raising agent, sugar or liquid; not baked long enough |
| Heavy, close texture | too little raising agent; flour beaten in instead of folded; too little creaming |
| Curdled mixture | eggs added too quickly or too cold |
| Dry and crumbly | too much flour; baked too long |

Prevention: weigh exactly, heat the oven before baking, add egg gradually, fold in the flour, and keep the oven door closed for the first part of baking.

variantes.nom: Importance of egg in a cake mixture
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to state a number of uses or functions of egg.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
1. It traps air when beaten, which makes the cake rise and light.
2. It sets (coagulates) in the oven and holds the structure.
3. It binds the ingredients together.
4. It gives colour and flavour.
5. It adds nutritive value (protein, vitamins and minerals).
6. The yolk contains lecithin, which helps fat and liquid to stay mixed.
Choose the exact number asked for.

sections.enonce_markdown: A recipe for a sandwich cake for 8 people uses 150 g margarine, 150 g sugar, 150 g self-raising flour and 3 eggs. A school needs 24 portions. (a) Calculate the quantity of each ingredient needed. (b) Name the method of mixing and describe its main stages.

etapes.justification: The quantities must be multiplied by the same number as the portions.
Every ingredient must be increased in the same proportion, or the cake would be spoilt.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Margarine, sugar and flour: $150 \times 3 = 450$ g each. Eggs: $3 \times 3 = 9$.

etapes.justification: Fat and sugar are beaten together and then eggs are added: this is the creaming method.
Each stage traps air or protects it.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Cream the fat and sugar until pale and fluffy. 2. Beat in the eggs a little at a time. 3. Fold in the sifted flour gently.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** Scale factor 3: **450 g margarine, 450 g sugar, 450 g flour and 9 eggs.** **(b)** The **creaming method**: cream the fat and sugar until pale and fluffy; beat in the eggs a little at a time to prevent curdling; fold in the sifted flour gently so that the air is kept; then bake in a preheated oven.

items.erreur_markdown: Adding all the eggs at once to the creamed fat and sugar.
items.pourquoi_faux: The mixture curdles because the egg cannot mix with the fat quickly; the cake becomes heavy.
items.correction_markdown: Add beaten egg a little at a time, beating well each time.

items.erreur_markdown: Opening the oven door early to see whether the cake has risen.
items.pourquoi_faux: Cold air enters and the cake, which has not yet set, sinks in the middle.
items.correction_markdown: Keep the door closed until the cake is nearly cooked.

items.erreur_markdown: Beating the flour hard into the creamed mixture.
items.pourquoi_faux: The air that was trapped is knocked out and the cake becomes heavy and tough.
items.correction_markdown: Fold in the sifted flour gently with a metal spoon.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that a cake which has risen and cracked on top was baked in an oven that was too cool.
items.pourquoi_faux: A too-hot oven sets the crust too soon; the middle then rises and splits it.
items.correction_markdown: Name oven too hot (or too much raising agent) as the cause; preheat and use the right temperature.

items.erreur_markdown: Making shortcrust pastry with warm hands, soft fat and plenty of water.
items.pourquoi_faux: The fat melts into the flour and the extra water develops the gluten, which gives hard, greasy pastry.
items.correction_markdown: Use cold fat, cool hands, a little cold water and light handling.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the method of cake making used in each case: (a) fat is rubbed into flour with the fingertips to make rock cakes; (b) eggs and sugar are whisked until thick and pale; (c) fat and sugar are beaten until pale and fluffy before the eggs are added.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Rubbing-in method**. (b) **Whisking method**. (c) **Creaming method**. (Award a mark for each.)

items.enonce_markdown: A baker uses 600 g of flour to make shortcrust pastry. (a) Calculate the weight of fat needed. (b) Margarine costs $2\,400$ FCFA per kilogram and flour costs $800$ FCFA per kilogram (assumed prices). Find the cost of the flour and fat.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Fat is half the weight of flour: $600 \div 2 = 300$, so **300 g** of fat. (b) Fat: 300 g = 0.3 kg, so $0.3 \times 2\,400 = 720$ FCFA. Flour: 600 g = 0.6 kg, so $0.6 \times 800 = 480$ FCFA. Total: $720 + 480 = 1\,200$, so **$1\,200$ FCFA**.

items.enonce_markdown: Cake A rose very high, cracked on top and was dark at the edges. Cake B sank in the middle and was sticky and damp inside. (a) Give two possible causes for each cake. (b) Explain why eggs should be added gradually when the creaming method is used. (c) State two ways in which sieving flour helps a cake.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Cake A: oven too hot; too much raising agent (or a tin that is too small). Cake B: oven door opened too early; too much raising agent, sugar or liquid; not baked long enough. (b) A large amount of egg added at once will not blend with the fat and sugar, so the mixture curdles and the cake is heavy. A little at a time keeps it smooth and holds in the air. (c) It adds air, and it removes lumps so that the flour mixes evenly with the other ingredients (it also mixes the raising agent evenly through the flour).

items_markdown: Four cake methods: creaming, rubbing-in, whisking, melting; know a short description and one example of each.
Eggs trap air, set the structure, bind, give colour and flavour, add nutrients.
Cracked top: oven too hot or too much raising agent; sunk middle: door opened early or underbaking; curdling: eggs added too fast.
Fold in flour gently and add egg gradually to keep the air in the mixture.
Shortcrust pastry: half as much fat as flour, cold fat and water, light handling, rest the dough, fairly hot oven.
When a recipe is scaled, multiply every ingredient by the same factor.
